invariants.rationale: UI frameworks commonly require non-negative width values; negative widths may not make sense for layout.
Similar to width, height is typically required to be non-negative in UI components.
If width is non-negative, adding it to x should not decrease the value, capturing layout logic.
If height is non-negative, adding it to y represents a layout span without underflow.
Ensures that neither width nor height are negative, which is often required in UI position/size semantics.
